narrative.overview:
Chain Calm is built for the operator who is already in the work — scanning for signals, ready to act. The interface is a dark, dense instrument. Every element earns its presence through operational necessity, not visual decoration. The atmosphere is that of a maritime control room or a NOC monitor wall: purposeful light in a dark environment, each illuminated element carrying meaning. Nothing glows that doesn't have a reason to glow.

The design language is restrained almost to severity. The dark navy-black surface (#080c16) recedes completely so that data has the foreground. Surface hierarchy is expressed through tonal steps — bg → card → popover are distinct tones at fixed distances, never shadows. Motion exists only when state changes: a badge shifting from amber to red, a panel sliding in, an ingest status pulsing. No choreography, no ambient animation.

This system explicitly rejects the idiom of typical SaaS analytics (purple-on-light, gradient-hero metrics, dashboard-as-marketing) and generic BI tool defaults (gray sidebar, flat blue bars, corporate-bland table styling). It is not a product demo — it is the thing a risk analyst stares at for a full shift.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy-black base surface with three distinct tonal layers
Single Inter family across all roles — no display/body split
Risk tier vocabulary (green / amber / red / deep-red) is the only non-neutral color on most screens
Primary blue (#3c83f6) reserved for actions, focus, and current selection — never decoration
Elevation expressed through background tone, never shadow
Motion confined to state transitions (150–250ms, ease-out-quart)

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Risk tier colors (risk-low, risk-medium, risk-high, risk-critical) are used exclusively to communicate disruption severity. They never appear as brand decoration, chart fills for neutral data, or background tints on non-risk UI. Their rarity is what makes them legible under pressure.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Primary (#3c83f6) appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Active nav item, primary CTA, focus ring. When everything is blue, nothing is a call to action.

rules.name: The Monotone Rule
rules.body: One family, differentiated by weight and size. Display fonts in buttons, labels, or data cells are prohibited — they introduce design-for-its-own-sake noise that degrades trust in a risk context.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: No fluid clamp() scaling. Product UI is viewed at consistent DPI on operator workstations. A fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar is worse, not better.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only on floating elements (dropdowns, tooltips, modals). Tonal differentiation — not shadow — is the language of layering in this system.

rules.name: The Semantic Glow Rule
rules.body: Colored glow is a state indicator, not decoration. The risk-glow utilities exist exclusively on risk-tier UI elements. Never apply them to decorative containers, feature cards, or marketing surfaces.

dos: Do use Action Blue (#3c83f6) only for interactive states: active nav, primary buttons, focus rings, and current selection indicators.
Do express depth through background tonal steps (Void → Panel Dark → Recessed → Overlay), not through box-shadow on content surfaces.
Do always pair a risk color with a text label or icon — never rely on color as the sole risk signal.
Do verify muted text contrast (Subdued #7588a3 = 5.0:1 on bg). Never go lower than this for body content.
Do reduce motion to instant transitions or crossfades under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do keep risk glow utilities exclusive to components that communicate risk severity.
Do use text-wrap: balance on panel headings and card titles.
Do build a semantic z-index scale: overlay (10) → dropdown (20) → sticky (30) → modal-backdrop (40) → modal (50) → toast (60) → tooltip (70).
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient background). The .text-gradient utility in index.css violates this rule and should be removed.
Don't use glassmorphism (backdrop-blur + semi-transparent backgrounds) as the default card surface. Reserve .glass-card for floating panels over live map content only.
Don't build an interface that looks like typical SaaS analytics — no purple-on-light themes, no gradient hero metrics, no big-number-small-label stat cards with gradient accents.
Don't use risk tier colors (green, amber, red, deep-red) for neutral data visualization or decorative fills.
Don't apply uppercase tracked labels as section kickers — one deliberate use is voice; eyebrows on every section heading is template scaffolding.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, margin, padding). Transform and opacity only.
Don't render dropdowns with position: absolute inside an overflow: hidden container — they will be clipped.
